project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable checkout under `gt_results/arvo_23153/_work/src/stb` is local merge commit `f54acd4e13430c5122cab4ca657705c84aa61b08`, whose `stb_image.h` line map matches the saved ASan crash (`3212` allocation, `3799` read). ARVO metadata instead reports upstream commit `c404b789ca01a00cd244240484f7eccdd639ef06`, and the staged `patch.diff` carries the later upstream fix logic from `5ba0baaa269b3fd681828e0e3b3ac0f1472eaf40`. This GT follows the staged source for all line-accurate locations and uses the metadata fix only as supporting evidence for the missing divisibility check.

classification.classification_note: ARVO metadata leaves this sample unclassified, but the saved sanitizer trace is a 1-byte heap out-of-bounds read from a JPEG component buffer.

bug_description.original: stb_image does not reject fractional JPEG component subsampling ratios. The component resamplers are not written to support this, and such ratios can appear in crafted JPEG files, leading to potential issues.
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged vulnerable source available here is older than the metadata commit pair, but the saved AddressSanitizer crash and the staged patch both close the same missing obligation: rejecting non-integral JPEG component subsampling ratios before MCU and resampler setup. The 207-byte witness begins with a short APP0 segment `ff e0 00 03 2a`, so `stbi__process_marker()` subtracts the APP length field and leaves only one payload byte, never setting `z->jfif`; the next APP14 marker stores Adobe color transform `0`. The later SOF0 header stores `img_y = 192`, `img_x = 200`, and `img_n = 3`, then parses component descriptors `01 22 00`, `02 31 01`, and `03 11 01`, so `z->rgb` stays `0` while the component sampling factors become `(2,2)`, `(3,1)`, and `(1,1)`. `stbi__process_frame_header()` then computes `h_max = 3` and `v_max = 2` but, in this staged revision, never performs the patch's divisibility check `h_max % h == 0` / `v_max % v == 0`. That leaves component 0 with a fractional horizontal ratio `3/2`. The same function commits `img_h_max = 3`, `img_v_max = 2`, computes `img_mcu_x = 9` and `img_mcu_y = 12`, sizes component 0 as `x = 134`, `y = 192`, `w2 = 144`, and `h2 = 192`, allocates the 27663-byte heap region reported by ASan, and publishes its aligned `data` pointer. Later `load_jpeg_image()` uses `z->app14_color_transform == 0 && !z->jfif` to make `is_rgb` true, truncates `3/2` to `hs = 1`, advances `line1` row by row across the 144-byte component plane, and on the last row the direct RGB copy loop still reads 200 pixels from that aliased row. Stage 01 reproduces AddressSanitizer's `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `load_jpeg_image:3799`, exactly 0 bytes past the 27663-byte allocation from `stbi__process_frame_header:3212`.

source.description: First project parser materialization of attacker-controlled state on the witnessed crashing path. APP marker parsing leaves `z->jfif` unset and records Adobe APP14 transform `0`, which later forces the malformed JPEG down the direct RGB copy path.
source.value_from: The exact 207-byte witness `gt_results/arvo_23153/poc` (sha256 `724da13422f717aa38b3873e233cb4b5f4129f6eeba06e78ec7baf2270b57b47`) begins `ff d8 ff ff ff ff ff ff e0 00 03 2a ... ff ee 00 0e 41 64 6f 62 65 00 01 01 00 04 00 00 ...`. For the APP0 marker, the parsed length `00 03` becomes `L = 1` after subtracting the length field, so the `L >= 5` JFIF branch is skipped and `z->jfif` stays `0`. The following Adobe APP14 bytes match the `Adobe\0` tag and set `z->app14_color_transform = 0`.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The direct RGB copy loop reads component-0 sample `y[i]` for all `img_x == 200` output pixels even though the aliased final component row comes from a plane whose stride is only `w2 == 144`.
sink.note: On the final row, `y` aliases the last component-0 row inside the heap object allocated at line 3212. The direct RGB loop still iterates `i = 0..199`, so it necessarily reads beyond the 27663-byte allocation after exhausting the 144-byte row plus alignment slack. AddressSanitizer reports that resulting 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read at `load_jpeg_image /src/stb/tests/../stb_image.h:3799:31`.

root_cause.description: The decoder derives global maxima from the component table and then continues as if every component were an integral divisor of those maxima; the later patch inserts the missing `h_max % h == 0` / `v_max % v == 0` rejection immediately after this loop.
root_cause.note: For the witness, this loop yields `h_max = 3` and `v_max = 2`. Component 0 still has `h = 2`, so its horizontal ratio is fractional (`3/2`) and should have been rejected before any MCU sizing or resampler setup.

tainted_value_origin.description: The raw 207-byte fuzzer input is installed as the JPEG parser's byte span; all later marker and header reads consume this exact `[buffer, buffer + 207)` range.

parser_admitted.description: After `stbi__decode_jpeg_header()` accepts SOI and processes the witness's short APP0 plus Adobe APP14 markers, the header scan reaches SOF0 and `stbi__process_frame_header()` admits the crafted component table to the JPEG decode path.

coarse_trace.summary: JPEG marker parsing resets the color-state fields, leaves `z->jfif == 0` because the APP0 segment is too short for the JFIF branch, and stores Adobe APP14 color transform `0`.
SOF0 parsing stores `img_y = 192`, `img_x = 200`, and `img_n = 3`, then materializes component ids `1,2,3` with sampling factors `(2x2)`, `(3x1)`, `(1x1)` while leaving `z->rgb == 0`.

The decoder derives `h_max = 3` and `v_max = 2` without the later divisibility check, commits `img_mcu_x = 9` and `img_mcu_y = 12`, sizes component 0 as `x = 134`, `y = 192`, `w2 = 144`, `h2 = 192`, allocates the 27663-byte heap object, and publishes its aligned `data` pointer.

Using the APP14/non-JFIF marker state, `is_rgb` becomes true; component 0's resampler truncates `3/2` to `hs = 1`, advances `line1` across the 144-byte plane one row at a time, and the identity helper aliases the final row as `y`.
The direct RGB copy loop still reads `y[i]` for `i < img_x == 200`, overrunning the last component-0 row and matching the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow at line 3799.

fine_trace.code:
s->img_buffer = s->img_buffer_original = (stbi_uc *) buffer;
s->img_buffer_end = s->img_buffer_original_end = (stbi_uc *) buffer+len;
fine_trace.note: Initializes the parser over the exact 207-byte PoC buffer, so every later JPEG marker and header read consumes attacker-controlled bytes from this span.
Before scanning markers, the decoder resets the JFIF/Adobe color-state fields that later control whether `load_jpeg_image()` uses direct RGB copy or YCbCr conversion.

Source. The witness's APP0 bytes `ff e0 00 03 2a` yield `L = 1` after subtracting the 2-byte length field, so the `L >= 5` JFIF branch is skipped and `z->jfif` remains `0` from step 1. The following APP14 bytes `ff ee 00 0e 41 64 6f 62 65 00 01 01 00 04 00 00` match Adobe APP14 and store `z->app14_color_transform = 0`.

SOF0 parsing materializes the witness's image geometry and component count as `img_y = 192`, `img_x = 200`, and `img_n = 3`. These values pass the local zero/count checks and later control plane sizing, the `is_rgb` predicate, `w_lores`, and the sink loop bound.

The following SOF0 component descriptors `01 22 00`, `02 31 01`, and `03 11 01` materialize ids `1,2,3` with sampling factors `(2,2)`, `(3,1)`, and `(1,1)`. Because `img_n == 3` from step 3 but the ids are not literal `R`,`G`,`B`, `z->rgb` stays `0`; each `h`/`v` still passes the local `1..4` validation, so component 0's non-divisor `h = 2` survives.

Root cause. The maxima become `h_max = 3` and `v_max = 2`, but this staged revision performs no divisibility check before proceeding. The later patch adds exactly that missing obligation here, rejecting any component where `h_max % h != 0` or `v_max % v != 0`.

fine_trace.var: z->img_h_max, z->img_v_max, z->img_mcu_w, z->img_mcu_h, z->img_mcu_x, z->img_mcu_y
fine_trace.note: Because the missing divisibility guard does not stop the decode, the maxima are committed into decoder state and used as if they were integral sampling ratios. For the witness this yields `img_h_max = 3`, `img_v_max = 2`, `img_mcu_w = 24`, `img_mcu_h = 16`, `img_mcu_x = 9`, and `img_mcu_y = 12`.

For component 0 (`h = 2`, `v = 2`) the unchecked maxima and MCU counts yield `x = 134`, `y = 192`, `w2 = 144`, and `h2 = 192`; line 3212 then allocates `144 * 192 + 15 = 27663` bytes. This is the heap region named by the saved ASan allocation stack.

The decoder turns the heap object from step 7 into the aligned base pointer later stored in `r->line0` and `r->line1`. Later row addressing is relative to this `data` pointer, not the original `raw_data` address.

With `img_n == 3` from step 3 and `z->rgb == 0` from step 4, the second disjunct controls the branch. Step 2 left `z->jfif == 0` and stored `z->app14_color_transform = 0`, so `is_rgb` becomes true and the decoder later takes the direct RGB copy path instead of YCbCr conversion.

fine_trace.var: r->hs, r->vs, r->ystep, r->w_lores, r->ypos, r->line0, r->line1, r->resample
fine_trace.note: For component 0 (`k = 0`), the unchecked fractional ratio is truncated by integer division to `r->hs = 3 / 2 = 1` and `r->vs = 1`. That sets `r->ystep = 0`, `r->w_lores = 200`, initializes both row pointers from step 8, and selects the identity `resample_row_1` path as if this plane were already full resolution.

Because `r->vs == 1`, this update block runs after every output row. Each time it promotes the current row to `line0`, increments `ypos`, and advances `line1` by `w2 = 144` while rows remain; after 191 completed rows, the next iteration uses `line1 = data + 191 * 144` for the final image row.

When the row loop calls the helper selected in step 10, `resample_row_1()` returns its `in_near` pointer unchanged. For the final row, that means `coutput[0]` and then `y` alias the advanced `r->line1` from step 11 instead of a separately bounded line buffer.

Sink. On the final row, `y` from step 12 aliases the last 144-byte component-0 row, but this loop still executes 200 iterations because `img_x == 200` from step 3 and `is_rgb` from step 9 selects the direct-copy path. The read therefore runs off the component-0 heap object from step 7 after exhausting that row and the allocator's alignment slack, matching the saved ASan `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at line 3799.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the crashing address is 0 bytes to the right of a 27663-byte region allocated here via `stbi__malloc_mad2(144, 192, 15)` for component 0.

poc.trigger: The exact 207-byte JPEG PoC starts with a short APP0 segment `ff e0 00 03 2a` that leaves `z->jfif == 0`, then an Adobe APP14 marker with transform `0x00`, and later an SOF0 component table `01 22 00 02 31 01 03 11 01`. In the staged decoder this yields `h_max = 3`, component 0 `h = 2`, truncated `hs = 1`, and the final direct-copy read past the component-0 allocation in `load_jpeg_image`.

format.name: jpeg
format.contract: The only trigger semantics established by the staged evidence are those of the exact 207-byte witness in `gt_results/arvo_23153/poc`: a JPEG whose early APP0 segment is `ff e0 00 03 2a` (too short to set `z->jfif`), whose Adobe APP14 marker sets color-transform byte `0x00`, and whose SOF0 bytes are `08 00 c0 00 c8 03 01 22 00 02 31 01 03 11 01`. In the staged v2.25 source this leaves `z->jfif == 0`, yields `h_max = 3` with component 0 `h = 2`, truncates `hs` to `1`, and reaches the final direct-copy read past the component-0 allocation. The saved artifacts do not justify a broader claim beyond this witness and the patch-stated divisibility obligation for fractional subsampling ratios.
